description: MonkeyMode guardrail preset: Bevy (Rust) under src/. Comments stay allowed (noComments false): Rust doc comments feed rustdoc and Clippy. Pair this with clippy.toml disallowed-methods for symbol-accurate checks (docs/engine/guardrails.md). Needs community verification: written from engine documentation knowledge, not field-tested in a MonkeyMode project yet.

rules.message: Sleeping inside a system blocks a scheduler thread and stalls the frame (and the server tick). Use a Timer component/resource, run conditions such as on_timer, or an AsyncComputeTaskPool task.
Blocking on a future inside the app blocks a scheduler thread. Spawn the work on IoTaskPool/AsyncComputeTaskPool and poll the Task in a system (future::poll_once / check_ready).

Raw threads are banned. They escape Bevy's scheduling and cannot touch the World. Use AsyncComputeTaskPool::get().spawn(...) or IoTaskPool and bring results back through a component or channel resource.
println!/dbg! are banned in game code. Agents judge behavior from logs, which needs levels and targets. Use bevy's info!/warn!/error!/debug! (tracing) with a target.

Exclusive systems taking &mut World are banned by default. They serialize the whole schedule and hide data dependencies from the scheduler. Use regular system parameters and Commands; if you truly need world access, propose it with the reason (user approval).

Changing virtual time speed or pausing Time<Virtual> is banned in networked games: peers drift and replicated simulation desyncs. Gate gameplay systems with a server-driven State or run condition instead. Remove this rule for single-player games (user approval).
